حَرِيثَةٌ : see حَرْثٌ. ＝
-A2- The pl., حَرَائِثُ, also signifies (assumed tropical:) Camels emaciated by travel: (El-Khattá- bee, K:) originally applied to horses: of camels you [generally] say, أَحْرَفْنَاهَا [“ we rendered them lean ”], with ف; and نَاقَةٌ حَرْفٌ means “ a lean she-camel. ” (El-Khattábee, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
